gap: No result ChatGPT got says how the coolers chill water. A compressor (the Avalon A4's 'highly efficient compressor', about 47 °F) gets water colder, chills it faster and uses less electricity than a thermoelectric (Peltier, also called 'electronic') unit, according to Embraco's refrigeration technical specialist. That is the thing to check before buying the 'small countertop electric cooler' type ChatGPT offered.
standout_why: I read Bob Vila (the only cited page), Shouldit and mybest. Bob Vila says 'Cooling mechanism: not stated' for all nine picks. Its only temperature figures are the Brio Moderna's 39 °F to 194 °F range. Shouldit measured litres of cold water per hour (A4 5.4 L/h, A8 2.7 L/h) but never says whether a unit uses a compressor or a thermoelectric module. Mybest gives one 47 °F figure for the Avalon B8 and nothing on how it cools. Popular Mechanics blocked my fetch, so I could not check it.
decides: It confirms the bottom-load pick: the Avalon A4 uses a compressor. That makes compressor-vs-thermoelectric the check that decides whether a cheap countertop unit will give properly cold water. ChatGPT's follow-up offered 'Small countertop electric cooler' without warning about this. It does not change the order among ChatGPT's bottom-load picks. I could not confirm on a maker page what the Brio 500 uses.

findings.value: Compressor coolers make water colder, cool it faster and use 'much less electricity' than Peltier (electronic) units
findings.source_title: Electronic Water Cooler: Myths And Facts – Embraco blog (Fernando Borba, Refrigeration Technical Specialist, 2014-01-02)
findings.note: Quotes: 'with a compressor, the cooler makes water colder and cools it faster'; 'Water coolers with compressors consume much less electricity than electronic ones'; Peltier wafers 'are more suitable for devices in which the need for refrigeration is very small'. Embraco makes compressors, so it has a stake in this comparison. The article is from 2014.
